subject: Re: Private deployment — DPA, customer-managed keys, and data access boundaries
messages:
From: Sarah Jenkins <sarah.jenkins@orionhealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alex Porter <alex.porter@orionhealth.com>
Date: 2026-02-10T09:12:00-05:00
Subject: Private deployment — initial DPA questions

Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We like the idea of Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem) for our PII workflows, but the legal and security team raised a few items before procurement can sign off. High-level asks:

- We need confirmation that customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) can be used such that Redwood personnel have no access to decryption keys.
- A clear subprocessor list and commitment to notify us 30 days before adding any new subprocessor that would access customer data.
- Clarification on data transfer mechanisms: we require EU->US transfers to be covered (SCCs or equivalent) and want wording about no persistent copies outside our VPC/on-prem instance.
- Auditability: monthly access logs and the ability to run a joint audit once a year.

Can you share the latest DPA and the subprocessors export? Procurement would like to start an initial review this week.

Thanks,
Sarah
Sarah Jenkins
Head of InfoSec, Orion Health

Attachment: requirements-summary.xlsx (referenced in body)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Jenkins <sarah.jenkins@orionhealth.com>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-02-11T11:03:00-05:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment — initial DPA questions

Hi Sarah — great to hear from you and glad the demo was useful. Attaching our current DPA draft (redwood-dpa-draft-v1.pdf) and a current snapshot of subprocessors (subprocessors-export-20260211.csv). Quick answers inline: 

- Customer-managed keys: supported. For Redwood Private we provide two patterns: 1) VPC deployment with KMS integration (customer key stored in their cloud KMS, we never persist the plaintext key) and 2) On-prem package where the customer supplies a local HSM and the inference nodes are configured to use that HSM via PKCS#11. In both cases we can add a clause that Redwood personnel are not authorized to retrieve or export customer keys.

- Subprocessors: the CSV lists third-party infra and telemetry vendors; current set includes: MetricsCo (monitoring), LogSink (log retention), and MirrorNet (network provider). We commit to 30 days' notice before any subprocessor that would have data-plane access. We can add a notification window and an objection right for your team in the DPA.

- Data transfers: for EU-origin data we use SCCs and will include a cross-border transfer addendum. For Private (VPC/on-prem) our standard setup is that no model outputs or logs are sent to Redwood-hosted analytics by default — those are optional and disabled unless you opt in. We'll document retention boundaries and default retention=0 for exported logs unless explicitly enabled.

- Auditability: we can provide monthly audit bundles (TLS-protected logs + signer verification) and a joint audit once annually. For on-prem we can provide an audit toolset and an audit checklist for remote or onsite audits.

Next steps: can we schedule a short call with your legal + our legal (copied: Stephanie) to agree DPA language? If you confirm procurement timeline we'll prioritize redlines and prepare a DocuSign packet.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-dpa-draft-v1.pdf; subprocessors-export-20260211.csv

Subject: RE: Private deployment — technical controls and limitations

Marissa / Steph — following up with the engineering perspective so legal can draft precise language. Key points for the DPA and SOW: 

- KMS/HSM integration: we support customer KMS via cloud provider KMS calls; we never store keys. For on-prem HSM we support PKCS#11 with a local agent that performs crypto operations and never exports keys. We should add an operational note that customer must rotate keys as needed; we can support automated key rotation hooks but rotation responsibility sits with the customer unless we agree to managed-key services (separate SOW).

- No-plain-text guarantee: we can commit that Redwood staff do not have access to plaintext model input/outputs in production unless a customer explicitly enables diagnostic collection. For troubleshooting, we require explicit written consent and can provide a timeboxed, access-audited session.

- Subprocessors with data-plane access: only MirrorNet (network) and LogSink (if enabled) have potential access vectors. MetricsCo only receives anonymized telemetry. We should be careful about describing 'access' — operationally, the inference nodes run inside the customer's VPC or on-prem and network egress is restricted by default.

- Audit logs: we can ship JSON log bundles (signed) monthly. For EU customers we'll ensure logs are stored in-region unless they choose cross-region export.

I'll prepare a short technical appendix for the DPA with exact API endpoints, auth headers, and a note about SCCs for EU transfers.

-rishi
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime

> On Feb 11, 2026, Marissa Cole wrote:
> > Hi Sarah — great to hear from you ...
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Jenkins <sarah.jenkins@orionhealth.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-02-13T14:22:00-05:00
Subject: RE: DPA redlines and notification windows

Hi Sarah — copying legal and ops. A few drafting proposals for procurement to consider: 

1) Subprocessor notification: Redwood will notify Orion Health at least 30 calendar days prior to onboarding a subprocessor that will have data-plane access; Orion will have 14 days to object on reasonable security/privacy grounds. If Orion objects, Redwood will either (a) not onboard for that Orion account, or (b) provide a remediation plan.

2) Access to keys: Add explicit clause: "Customer-held keys: Redwood acknowledges that customer-controlled encryption keys are under the exclusive control of the customer; Redwood personnel shall not access, export, or persist plaintext encryption keys or decrypted customer data except as explicitly authorized in writing for troubleshooting and only under time-limited, auditable sessions."

3) Data transfer language: For EU-origin data, Redwood will execute SCCs and provide a transfer addendum indicating the technical safeguards (in-region logging, encryption in transit and at rest, documented subprocessor locations).

4) Auditability & retention: Default logs retention for Private is 0 days for persisted logs; optional analytics exports must be opt-in. Monthly audit packages will include signed access logs, configuration snapshot, and a summary of any personnel access requests in the period.

If those points look OK we can prepare redlines and send to Sarah's procurement team.

Thanks,
Stephanie Nguyen
VP Legal & Trust, Redwood Inference

Date: 2026-02-17T15:45:00-05:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment — final questions before redlines

Marissa / team — thanks for the clear breakdown and the attachments. A few follow-ups from procurement: 

- DocuSign: once legal finalizes redlines we will sign via DocuSign. Please prepare the packet and include the transfer addendum.
- Subprocessor CSV: we noticed MirrorNet is US-based; confirm that for EU-hosted instances MirrorNet's network hops will not route egress through US-based peering without SCCs in place.
- Managed-key option: procurement is open to a managed-key SOW if Redwood provides an MSSP-like SLA for key rotation and recovery; please include a ballpark number for the SOW so we can budget.

Can you send redlines by EOD Friday (2026-02-20) so we can route through our legal?

Thanks,
Alex Porter
Procurement, Orion Health
